what_it_does: Large AI models trained on many tasks and data types (text, images, audio, etc.) at once — called multi-task, multi-modal foundation models — are harder to train efficiently than single-task models because different components finish their work at different speeds, leaving some processors idle while others are still busy. Spindle addresses this by breaking the training work into groups of small sub-tasks called 'waves' and then running them in a pipelined fashion — like a factory assembly line where different stations work on different waves simultaneously. It first figures out how to split work across chips given that different modalities (e.g., processing an image versus processing text) require very different amounts of compute, and then it schedules overlapping execution so that one wave's computation fills the gap while another wave waits for its data.
